decisions.rationale: In 'common FRDA point mutation', FRDA is a disease name used to modify the noun 'mutation', so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than a standalone disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'Friedreich ataxia' names one specific disease with no further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1: Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: This is the abbreviation 'FRDA' in '( FRDA )' that defines the synonym of 'Friedreich ataxia'. Per the abbreviation rule, the short form is annotated as a separate mention of the same Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §6: Annotate all synonymous mentions (abbreviation definitions)

decisions.rationale: 'inherited ataxia' refers to a family of multiple specific diseases rather than one defined disease, so it is a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1: Disease Class mentions (family of multiple specific diseases)

decisions.rationale: Here FRDA is the name of the gene ('the affected gene, FRDA'), not a disease mention, so it should not be annotated as a disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1: only mentions referring to a disease name are annotated

decisions.rationale: In 'exon 4 of FRDA', FRDA refers to the gene location, not to the disease, so it is not a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1: only mentions referring to a disease name are annotated

decisions.rationale: In 'an atypical FRDA phenotype', FRDA is a disease name modifying the noun 'phenotype', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
